out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: - OBSERVED: rehydrated seaweed (71f) was stored on speed rack for about 1.5 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated the CFM on cold holding. CFM cooked the seaweed immediately.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: grilled seasoned squid (39f) was prepared on 9/11/2026 and stored in walk-in cooler without date marking. Cooked mushroom (38f) was stored in walk-in cooler without date marking. CFM was not able to identify its preparation date.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: CFM discarded the squid. EHS prompted CFM to discard the cooked mushroom.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Clean and Sanitize
violations.observation: There is no certified food manager on duty and the person in charge failed to explain the correct procedures for cleaning and sanitizing utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment. - OBSERVED: a food employee added bleach solution to wash, rinse and sanitize basin at 3-compartment sink to clean containers.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall know that all utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be 1) washed with hot, soapy water to remove visible soil, 2) rinsed to remove residue, 3) sanitized using an approved sanitizer to reduce the number of bacteria and viruses and 4) air dried. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated the food employee and prompted CFM to provide necessary training.

out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. - OBSERVED: CFM was not on site at the beginning of inspection. out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: - OBSERVED: working containers for salt and sugar stored on prep table were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. - EHS prompted CFM to label the containers properly.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: - OBSERVED: small cups were used to dispense sugar and salt stored on prep table.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated CFM and prompted CFM to use spoon to dispense condiments.

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: Food Establishmend Prohibited from ROP of Fish
violations.observation: The following fresh, not frozen, fish are packaged using the Reduced Oxygen Packaging (ROP) method: SALMON.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment may not package fresh fish (raw, unfrozen) using a ROP method. EHS EDUCATED THE CFM. CFM WILL NOT PACKAGE FRESH FISH USING A ROP METHOD.

violations.title: ROP, HACCP Plan in Place
violations.observation: The establishment does not have an approved HACCP plan for the food that is packaged using the Reduced Oxygen Packaging (ROP) process. BONE BROTH, CRAB MEAT, SPICY CRAB MEAT, AND PORK.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment that packages a time/temperature control for safe food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method shall have a HACCP plan that contains the information specified under 8-201.14(D) and that: 1) identifies the food to be packaged, 2) requires that the packaged food shall be maintained at 41F or less, has a water activity of 0.91 or less, a pH of 4.6 or less, is a meat or poultry product that is cured at a food processing plant, is received in an intact package, or is a food with a high level of competing organisms, 3) describes how the package shall be prominently and conspicuosly labeled on the principal display panel in bold type on a contrasting background with instructions to maintain the food at 41F or below and discard the food if within 14 calendar days of its packaging, 40 limits the refrigerated shelf life to no more than 14 calendar days from packaging to consumption or the origjnal manufacturer's 'sell by' or 'use by' date whichever occurs first, 5) includes operational procedures that prohibit contacting food with bare hands, identifies a designated work area and the method by which physical barriers or methods of separation minimizes cross contamination, access to the processing equipment is limited to responsible trained personnel, and cleaning and sanitizing procedures for equipment/utensils is monitored, and 6) describes the training program that ensures that the individual responsible for the ROP operation understands the concepts required for a safe operation, understands the equipment and facilites, and procedures specified in this section. (1) IMMEDIATELY STOP SERVING ROP PACKAGED FOODS TO CUSTOMERS. (2) IMMEDIATELY STOP PACKAGING FOOD USING ROP METHOD. (3) CFM WILL SUBMIT A HACCP PLAN TO HEALTH DEPARTMENT FOR APPROVAL.
